functions.name: core_i2c_handle_for_bus
functions.signature: core_i2c_handle_for_bus(uint8_t bus)
functions.brief: The I2C handle for a bus id declared in config.json, or NULL if the project doesn't declare that bus. Emitted per project by coregen into core_init.c (when the project declares any I2C bus); the *_bus helpers below resolve their handle through it. Forward-declared here rather than `#include "core_init.h"` so this header compiles without a project (val tests, examples without config.json). The natives-side caller is gated on CORE_HAS_I2C_BUSES, so the linker never asks for the symbol unless the dispatcher exists.

functions.name: ll_i2c_init
functions.signature: ll_i2c_init(I2C_TypeDef * i2c, uint32_t timing)
functions.brief: Initialize I2C in master mode. i2c:     I2C instance timing:  TIMINGR value (use LL_I2C_TIMING_* defines) fmp:     set non-zero to enable Fast-mode Plus (CR1.FMP bit) Only effective on STM32WBA55 and STM32H523. On L422, FMP is enabled via SYSCFG — see ll_i2c_init_fmp(). On L011, FMP is not supported.

functions.name: ll_i2c_init_fmp
functions.signature: ll_i2c_init_fmp(I2C_TypeDef * i2c, uint32_t timing)
functions.brief: Initialize I2C in Fast-mode Plus (1 MHz), with the Fm+ (20 mA) pad drive. WBA55 / H523: I2C_CR1.FMP (bit 24). L422: I2C_CR1 bits 31:24 are reserved (RM0394 §38.9.1); Fm+ drive is SYSCFG_CFGR1.I2C1_FMP (bit 20) / I2C3_FMP (bit 22), RM0394 §9.2.2, which needs the SYSCFG clock (RCC_APB2ENR.SYSCFGEN, bit 0).

functions.name: ll_i2c_write
functions.signature: ll_i2c_write(I2C_TypeDef * i2c, uint8_t addr, const uint8_t * data, uint32_t len)
functions.brief: Master write to a 7-bit address device. addr:  7-bit slave address (unshifted, e.g. 0x68 for MPU6050) data:  pointer to bytes to send len:   number of bytes Returns LL_I2C_OK on success, LL_I2C_NACK, LL_I2C_ERROR, or LL_I2C_TIMEOUT on failure.

functions.name: ll_i2c_read
functions.signature: ll_i2c_read(I2C_TypeDef * i2c, uint8_t addr, uint8_t * buf, uint32_t len)
functions.brief: Master read from a 7-bit address device. addr:  7-bit slave address (unshifted) buf:   buffer to store received bytes len:   number of bytes to read Returns LL_I2C_OK on success, LL_I2C_NACK, LL_I2C_ERROR, or LL_I2C_TIMEOUT on failure.

functions.name: ll_i2c_target_init
functions.signature: ll_i2c_target_init(I2C_TypeDef * i2c, uint32_t timing, uint8_t addr7)
functions.brief: Initialize I2C as a target (device) at a 7-bit own address. i2c:     I2C instance timing:  TIMINGR value (use LL_I2C_TIMING_* defines). A target does not drive SCL, but TIMINGR still sets SDADEL/SCLDEL, which govern data setup and hold. Use the constant matching the controller's speed. addr7:   7-bit own address, unshifted (e.g. 0x28) Enables address-match, RX, TX, NACK, STOP and error interrupts. The caller still has to unmask the IRQ in the NVIC.

functions.name: ll_i2c_target_disable
functions.signature: ll_i2c_target_disable(I2C_TypeDef * i2c)
functions.brief: Stop answering on the bus and release the own address.

functions.name: ll_i2c_target_is_read
functions.signature: ll_i2c_target_is_read(I2C_TypeDef * i2c)
functions.brief: Direction of the transfer the controller just addressed us for. Returns 1 when the controller intends to READ from us (we transmit), 0 when it intends to write. Only meaningful while ADDR is set.

functions.name: ll_i2c_target_addcode
functions.signature: ll_i2c_target_addcode(I2C_TypeDef * i2c)
functions.brief: The 7-bit address that actually matched. Worth reading when OAR2 or address masking puts more than one address on the same peripheral.

functions.name: ll_i2c_target_flush_tx
functions.signature: ll_i2c_target_flush_tx(I2C_TypeDef * i2c)
functions.brief: Discard a byte still sitting in TXDR. TXE is write-1-to-flush. Always do this before answering a read. A controller that abandoned a previous read (or NACKed early) can leave a stale byte loaded, and without a flush that byte is the first thing the next read receives, shifting the whole transfer by one.

functions.name: ll_i2c_target_clear_addr
functions.signature: ll_i2c_target_clear_addr(I2C_TypeDef * i2c)
functions.brief: Clear the address match, which releases the stretched SCL.
